title: MPs ask what the break clause was for as Palantir wins two more years in the NHS
html:
TOP STORIES

  • China’s grip on Top500 remains uncontested as US chases AI-HPC fusion

    In the age of AI, the top spot on the bi-annual ranking is whoever willing to run HPL instead of LLMs

  • US allies deepen deal to guard AI supply chains against 'hostile actors' (cough, China, cough)

    Securing supply chains or coercing other nations to help Washington sideline Beijing and its AI ambitions?

  • Marvell and Penguin Solutions aim to end the RAMpocalypse with photonic memory fabric

    Appliances can share 16 TB of DRAM and half a terabyte of HBM across up to 16 systems

  • Elon Musk leads Silicon Valley's campaign to put Jensen Huang back in charge at Nvidia

    More than 173,000 signatures, a few famous billionaires, and absolutely no guarantee they're genuine

  • Chinese AI labs are training models on Nvidia's Blackwell despite export controls, says ex-OpenAI engineer

    Forensic report finds Blackwell's fingerprint in DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group models

  • Security

    Russians are posing as Signal support to launch phishing attacks

    PLUS: US takes down Iranian propaganda sites; Marketing company asks 'Why Do We Have Your Information?' And more!

  • Security

    Microsoft patches failed to fix on-prem SharePoint, which is now under zero-day attack

    PLUS: China upgrades smartphone surveillance tools; Ring eases anti-snooping stance; and more

  • Black Hat and DEF CON

    DEF CON Franklin project enlists hackers to harden critical infrastructure

    Voting village reports have been so successful, says Jeff Moss, that the whole of DEF CON will now be included

  • Security

    EQT buys majority share in Swiss cybersecurity biz Acronis

    Went at equivalent of $3.5B+ valuation for entire firm, though portion sold not specified

  • Malware Month

    Ten years since the first corp ransomware, Mikko Hyppönen sees no end in sight

    On the plus side, infosec's a good bet for a long, stable career

  • Omaxian takes the Omarchy look down a different Linux backstreet

    Devuan-based distro swaps Wayland for XLibre and i3, with Xfce waiting if the tiling gets tiresome

  • Microsoft’s Azure Linux dons Fedora to dress itself up for mainstream workloads

    Version 4.0 of Redmond’s cloudy OS is free to use in its cloud. Repeat. Free to use

  • Another Linux kernel developer steps back from some duties due to overload

    You can probably guess what he blames for the excessive workload

  • The latest FreeBSD report is here, and the AI debate is ongoing

    Only a minority want to ban it. Plus plenty of updates on 16 projects

  • Orbit Global Menu: A working global menu addon for GNOME

    We love this, but suspect this is the Marmite of GNOME extensions

  • Crowd fave Linux Mint update approaches, fresh from autumn release of Cinnamon desktop

    Mint 27 to land before Christmas, with stable Wayland display upgrades, as punters try out Cinnamon 6.8
summary: Ministers promise fresh procurement, but critics warn extension gives US supplier more time to dig in
